runtimes.name: Wine Stable 11.0
runtimes.summary: Mainline Wine, four major versions newer than the bundled engine. No D3DMetal, so it isn't the right choice for demanding games — but it's the current reference point for anything the older engine can't run, the Steam client above all.

runtimes.name: Sikarugir Wine 11.0
runtimes.summary: Wine 11 built for DXMT, so it has both modern Wine and Direct3D 11 on Metal — the combination nothing else here has. Installs and reports its version, but on some Macs cannot create a container at all: every Windows process it starts is killed by macOS the moment Wine hands control to Windows code. Try it, and keep Wine Stable if it can't boot.

runtimes.name: Wine 11.16 (DXMT)
runtimes.summary: Wine 11.16 from winehq source with CodeWeavers' winemac.drv patch, so a Direct3D 11 swap chain has a CAMetalLayer to present into. Built rather than downloaded because no published build has both that and a prefix that boots here. Also the only build with a real i386 architecture (--enable-archs=i386,x86_64) rather than 32-on-64, which is what 32-bit games with deep call stacks need. Compiled without gnutls, so Windows code running inside the installation gets no TLS — which games do not use, because the store client and the launcher both live outside it.

games.note: Retina Mode off: with it on, Prey's 2048×1330 fullscreen is rendered into a quarter of a 4096×2660 desktop and every display gets captured.

AMD's Display Library disabled: the game asks Wine's atiadlxx for the graphics adapter, Wine's copy is a stub that succeeds without producing a context, and the game reads through the null it is handed — 'Unhandled page fault on read access to 00000050'. The logo appears and the process is gone. Disabled rather than stubbed differently, because a DLL that fails to load sends the game down its 'no such hardware' path, which is the truth on a Mac. Native d3dcompiler as well, which is what the winetricks verbs are for: past the adapter query the game compiles its shaders at runtime and Wine's own HLSL compiler cannot ('Unhandled instruction type HLSL_IR_JUMP' for every shader with a branch), then faults on the shader thread two disclaimers in. It imports 43, not 47 — BioshockHD.exe names D3DCOMPILER_43.dll in its import table — and both are 'n,b', never a bare 'n': 'n' is native-only, so a failed verb download would mean the game will not start at all rather than merely losing the fix.

Needs a Wine with a real i386 architecture, which on this catalogue means the DXMT build. On the bundled engine — CrossOver-derived and therefore 32-on-64, where every Win32 call reaches the 64-bit side through a thunk and the frames come out deeper than this game was built for — pressing Escape through the opening cinematic exhausts the main thread's stack: an exception frame twelve kilobytes below the bottom of a 1MB stack, then 'NtRaiseException Exception frame is not in stack limits'. Retina Mode off, unlike the earlier note here: turning it on also stopped the crash, but only by taking every attached display into backing mode, which blanks the second monitor. The runtime is the fix; Retina Mode was a symptom.
